actor.description: Recorded actor identity, not host-authenticated authority.

file.description: A staged file relative to the work directory. The consumer verifies its actual bytes against sha256.

relativePath.description: A slash-separated file path relative to the work directory; no absolute path, dot segment, parent traversal, drive prefix or backslash.

context.description: Supporting notes and reference files used to understand the task, separate from its inputs. Empty collections explicitly mean no extra context. Context does not grant additional execution authority.
context.title: Request context

decision.description: .works/<workId>/decisions/<id>.json: an attributed decision on an exact work revision and subject digest. Identity and authority are not authenticated by this schema.
decision.title: Decision

evidence.description: .works/<workId>/evidence/<id>.json: artifact metadata. Existence, actual digest and evidentiary relevance require separate checks.
evidence.title: Evidence

index.description: Version 1 of the proposed .works document format. A document must match exactly one kind. This contract does not migrate or reinterpret legacy session records.
index.title: Works document contract

inputs.description: The prompts and files the request asks the skill to act on. At least one prompt or file is required.
inputs.title: Request inputs

output.description: One produced output. Text is inline; commits identify a repository and full object ID; images and other files bind persisted artifacts. Output metadata alone does not prove correctness or publication.
output.title: Response output

request.description: .works/<workId>/requests/<id>.json: prompts and files to act on, with supporting context kept separate, against one work revision. This record alone grants no execution permission.
request.title: Request

response.description: .works/<workId>/responses/<id>.json: typed outputs produced for one request. Optional verification observations describe their checks separately; delivering an output is not a claim that the work is proved complete.

feedbackRound.description: Completed feedback-and-repair rounds for this request. Initial candidate is round zero; the caller maintains truthful history.

response.title: Response

work.description: .works/<id>/work.json: goal, declared scope, acceptance criteria and current lifecycle.
work.title: Work

@cli/curl.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/curl.note: On Windows resolve the curl executable (curl.exe), not a PowerShell alias with different argument semantics. A native web-fetch capability is not this CLI alias.
@cli/curl.purpose: Probe an HTTP endpoint using the curl executable.

@cli/python.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/python.note: Resolve Python 3 from the active environment: python, python3, or py -3 as appropriate; record the selected executable and any launcher arguments.

@tools/browsercontrol.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/browsercontrol.purpose: Drive a real browser against a served route: navigate, act, capture screenshots and DOM measurements.

claude.via: mode required: the in-app Browser pane, or Claude in Chrome when the task needs the person's sessions

openai.via: mode required: Codex computer use, which opens the person's own Chrome, on a dedicated browser profile (the shared UAT identity), never the person's logged-in profile

@tools/fileread.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/fileread.purpose: Read declared workspace files and directories through the active session.

claude.via: Claude Code Read, Glob and Grep

@tools/sourcewrite.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/sourcewrite.purpose: Edit files within the declared write scope through the active session.

@workspaces/artifacts.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/artifacts.purpose: Produced files, including images, documents and other deliverables.

@workspaces/context.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/context.purpose: Supporting reference files for a request.

@workspaces/inputs.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/inputs.purpose: Files supplied as the subject of a request.

@workspaces/requests.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/requests.purpose: Requests with separate inputs and context.

@workspaces/responses.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/responses.purpose: Responses declaring produced outputs and execution status.

criteria.stopWhen: Return done only when all criteria and criteriaResults pass. Block on uncertain identity effects or missing authority. Stop after two feedback rounds or an unchanged repeated failure.

purpose: Provision or repair the identities for one declared flow at its bound provider, prove provider state and real sign-in, and publish a secret-free account record.

request.description: inputs.prompts identify provision or rotation, provider and realm, authorization, environment, exact aliases, roles, memberships, credential name and mutable resource ceiling. inputs.files hold the approved desired state; context files hold provider, route and custody records. Credential values are forbidden.
request.title: identity.provision request

response.description: A done provisioning response contains a secret-free delta, proof set and account record. A rotation may use account-record as a secret-free rotation record and must not claim a flow account was created.
response.title: identity.provision response

scope: Only accounts, roles and memberships enumerated by the supplied desired state at one provider and realm. It may rotate one explicitly bound credential as a separate operation. It does not seed data, operate runtimes, write provider configuration, or record credential values.

calls.purpose: Read approved desired state and typed provider, route and custody context.

steps.instruction: Read request, approved desired state and typed provider/custody context. Freeze operation, provider, realm, environment, aliases, roles, memberships, credential name, mutable ceiling and sign-in endpoint. Reject credential values and ask for missing authority.
produces: A frozen provider operation and account set.

reads.when: when a desired-state file is declared

calls.purpose: Run only the declared provider inventory requests against the supplied external provider context.

steps.instruction: Query the externally identified provider by stable account reference and username. Classify every alias reusable, missing, invalid or uncertain; observe provider, realm, role and memberships before any mutation. For rotation, bind exactly one existing principal.

calls.purpose: Apply only the approved provider effects using credential values without recording them.
calls.when: after a safe delta is known

steps.instruction: Reuse correct accounts, create missing accounts, and repair only wrong provider-owned role, membership or credential state. Resolve the credential by name only at the request boundary. After an uncertain effect, inventory by stable reference and username before retrying. Never create a duplicate.

calls.purpose: Read provider roles and memberships without exposing secrets.
Perform a fresh real login through the bound product endpoint.
Persist secret-free proof, account and response records.
Validate the compiled operator request and response.

steps.instruction: Read provider state and perform fresh real product sign-in for each flow alias. For rotation, prove the new credential works and the old fails. Write secret-free checks and account records, evaluate concrete feedback, repair only the failing provider field, and return done only after reassessment accepts every criterion.

validate.failurePolicy: Inventory identities before mutation and after uncertain effects. Feedback names the exact account field or proof failure; repair only that provider-owned field and reassess. Never create a duplicate account to escape uncertainty.

review.instruction: Compare provider, realm, aliases, roles, memberships and mutations with the approved desired state and mutable resource ceiling. Reject self-granted authority or unrequested identities.
Require stable provider references, observed roles and memberships, and a fresh real sign-in through the bound product endpoint for every account. Token issuance alone is insufficient.
For credential rotation, require the bound principal, new credential success and old credential failure; reject duplicate principals or a rotation combined with account provisioning.
Inspect all records and transcripts. They may contain credential names and custody references but no credential values, tokens, handles or reusable secret-shaped material.
